text:
Jake DeBrusk's story in Vancouver is mostly about where he'd rather be. The Fourth Period has reported, and Markerzone and Vancouver Hockey Daily have passed along, that his stance hasn't changed: he would rather not be part of a Canucks rebuild. Markerzone notes he holds a full no-movement clause, so any move runs through him. Heavy.com went as far as calling his fate with the Canucks "All But Officially Sealed."

On the ice he's been unlucky more than bad. He has five goals on 7.1 expected in 18 games, and the chances keep coming: four shots and 0.76 expected goals in Monday's loss to Philadelphia alone. His rate of quality chances, 1.40 expected goals per 60, is close to last season's, when he scored 23. The Canucks also get a better share of play at five-on-five with him than without. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 55% of his shots coming off the rush, so he lives on transition, which is hard to find on a team that has lost nine of its last ten. If the goals catch up to the chances, his value only goes up.
headline: DeBrusk is due, and his future is elsewhere
